items.followUp: Define amorphous solids and give two examples.

rubric.why: A regular, orderly arrangement of particles is the defining feature of crystalline solids.
rubric.description: Defines crystalline solids by the arrangement of their particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear definition that describes an ordered arrangement of particles.

rubric.why: The question asks for examples as well as the definition.
rubric.description: Gives two valid examples of crystalline solids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct examples.

modelAnswer: Crystalline solids are solids whose particles are arranged in a regular, orderly pattern.
Examples include sodium chloride and quartz.

rubric.why: Condensation is the change of state from gas to liquid.
rubric.description: Identifies the change from a gas or vapour into a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the change of state.

rubric.why: Cooling or loss of heat brings about condensation.
rubric.description: States that condensation occurs when the gas or vapour is cooled or loses heat.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning cooling or heat loss.

modelAnswer: Condensation is the change of a gas or vapour into a liquid.
It occurs when the gas or vapour is cooled or loses heat.

rubric.why: The m/v percentage expresses the mass of solute per 100 mL of solution.
rubric.description: Defines m/v % as grams of solute in 100 mL of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly relating solute mass to 100 mL of solution.

rubric.why: A valid numerical example shows how the concentration unit is used.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as 5 g of glucose in 100 mL of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example with the mass and volume.

modelAnswer: The m/v % concentration is the number of grams of solute present in 100 mL of solution.
For example, a 5% m/v glucose solution contains 5 g of glucose in 100 mL of solution.

items.followUp: What is an alloy? Give one example.

rubric.why: Alloying is the process of combining a metal with other element(s) to form an alloy.
rubric.description: Describes alloying as mixing a metal with one or more other elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the materials combined in alloying.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates the definition.
rubric.description: Gives one valid example of an alloy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct alloy example.

modelAnswer: Alloying is the process of mixing a metal with one or more other elements, usually in the molten state, to form an alloy.
Brass, made from copper and zinc, is an example.

items.followUp: Why are copper and iron more reactive than gold?

accept: low tendency to form positive ions
rubric.why: Silver and gold are least reactive because they do not readily lose electrons to form positive ions.
rubric.description: Explains their low reactivity in terms of their low tendency to lose electrons or form positive ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating this explanation.

rubric.why: Their position near the bottom of the reactivity series or occurrence in the native state supports their low reactivity.
rubric.description: Gives a supporting fact about their position in the reactivity series or occurrence uncombined in nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid supporting fact.

modelAnswer: Silver and gold have a very low tendency to lose electrons and form positive ions.
They are near the bottom of the reactivity series and may occur in the native state.
